# cyber:cyber

> An independent studio shaping brands and building distinctive digital products. Founded and led by Dan Andrews in London.

cyber:cyber is Dan Andrews’s independent studio in London. Granite, Kaido and Frame are products owned, designed and built by the studio; selected commissions sit alongside them. The work connects identity, interface and implementation. Scope, deliverables and the allocation of time are agreed for each engagement.

The studio's owned products are central to its practice: Kaido (clinical rehab planning), Granite and Frame (native iOS apps), all designed and built in-house, plus one delivered client engagement (IKARAO, for Bittensor). The cases show product captures and generated identity output. Kaido screens are captured from the current running app using fictional local demo patients; they do not report clinical outcomes.

The site itself is hand-coded vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no build step and no framework — one self-contained file per page. That is a deliberate position, argued in the journal note "The hardest client was us".

## Core

- [Home](https://www.cybercyber.ai/): Independent design and development, the work, and the engagement options.
- [Manifesto](https://www.cybercyber.ai/manifesto.html): Working commitments linked to practical evidence from the studio's work.
- [Journal](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal.html): Working notes on product decisions, interaction design and building software.
- [The Register](https://www.cybercyber.ai/specimen.html): The house type specimen published as law — one variable face, seven permitted weights, eight sizes, a seeded setting machine, and the measured drift the rules haven't caught up with.

## Work

- [Kaido](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-kaido.html): Criteria-based rehab planning for physiotherapy clinics. Patients, rehabilitation plans and progress in one clinic workspace. An independent owned product in a private clinic pilot, with web and native iOS surfaces. It does not use Granite's engine.
- [Granite](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-granite.html): A native, on-device strength coach for athletes whose sport isn't lifting. Owned product at alpha stage, connecting weekly planning, coach input, session execution and on-device history.
- [Frame](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-frame.html): An owned native jiu-jitsu training journal at alpha stage. Session capture, training history and a position-based technique library form the intended product loop; learning and retention outcomes are not claimed.
- [IKARAO](https://www.cybercyber.ai/work-ikarao.html): A generative identity system for Bittensor, combining art direction, deterministic drawing code, specimen sheets and application templates. Commissioned scope delivered; application examples include labelled concepts. The other three cases are owned products.

## Journal

- [The sea lion papers](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-sea-lion.html): Ninety fabricated research citations, caught by checking every one against PubMed — and what a clinical product owes a clinician after that.
- [The word before it drifted](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-the-word.html): cyber comes from the Greek for helmsman, and "governor" is the same word by a different road — what that means for a studio whose products are literally feedback loops with a human at the wheel.
- [The hardest client was us](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-hardest-client.html): Why the studio's own site was treated as the hardest brief of the year — hand-built, with product captures and presentation studies clearly distinguished.
- [Nobody wrote it down](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-undocumented.html): On confabulation, contextual inquiry, and why almost no software will make a decision.
- [The velocity gods](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-velocity.html): How speed stopped being a means and became a faith — what the cult of shipping fast produces, and what it costs.
- [Building cyber:cyber](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-building.html): A historical working note on building the studio, with a correction reflecting current product stages and presentation.
- [Shipping got commoditised](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-shipping.html): Anyone can ship a product in a weekend now. What's actually scarce once production is free.
- [Six things native AI features get right](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-six-things.html): The six decisions that separate native AI from a chat bubble in the corner.
- [Why cyber:cyber exists](https://www.cybercyber.ai/journal-why.html): The founding note on independent product work and design judgement.

## The offer

- Product Direction — £5,000 per week. One or two weeks to resolve the proposition and core workflow, with a focused prototype and scoped next step.
- Product Release — from £50,000 for a scoped release or substantial redesign. Deliverables, platforms, integrations and handover are agreed upfront.
- Design Partnership — from £12,000 per month. An agreed allocation for product direction, interface work and implementation support.

## Who

- Dan Andrews — designer, London. A decade across brand, interface, motion and interaction, including Spotify, Epic Games and Dell, and early-stage teams before and since. Drawn to complex domains — the kind where you have to learn the subject before you can design in it. Personal site: [iamdanandrews.com](https://iamdanandrews.com).
- There is no bench and no account team; the person who designs it is the person who builds it.

## Contact

- Email: hello@cybercyber.ai — one sentence about what you're trying to ship is enough. Enquiries go directly to Dan.
